# Kpler & GrowthBook | Enterprise Setup Conversation
Date: 2026-09-16 | Duration: 56m

## Summary
The Lufthansa RFP remains ongoing, with answers needed by tomorrow, while overlapping meetings with the Capilla team created scheduling conflicts. The team discussed heavy feature-flag usage and limited experimentation, noting that internal users currently rely on frontend overrides to toggle flags individually. This workaround lacks a backend source of truth, and a client SDK feature for patching flag values per user is missing. There is interest in moving from Pro to Enterprise by October 31; Enterprise includes SSO, SAML, stable pricing, and training support. The Pro plan’s pricing will change soon, with a grandfathering period available, but internal budget approval and stakeholder alignment are still needed, primarily through Rémi Becheras. Marcel will send a summary email and pricing examples the next day. A follow-up with PMs and the customer success head is planned for October 24 afternoon to clarify feature flags, experimentation workflow, and adoption support. Philippe can help coordinate SSO internally.

## Keywords
feature flagging, GrowthBook, enterprise plan, experimentation, SSO, seat usage

## Action Items
**Rémi Becheras**  
Discuss experimentation goals internally (32:11)  
Investigate seat usage at Kpler (32:11)  
Decide on supporting individual user toggling (27:47)  
Confirm GrowthBook budget owner (35:22)  

**Marcel Geldner**  
Investigate individual user toggling with GrowthBook (25:37)  
Discuss toggling priority with GrowthBook founders (35:47)  
Provide Enterprise pricing examples (36:41)  
Send summary email to Kpler (38:34)  
Schedule follow-up meeting for October 24th (44:20)  

**Rémy Marin**  
Follow up on feature flagging overrides (25:37)

# KPLER & GrowthBook | Contract Finalisation
Date: 2026-10-28 | Duration: 20m

## Summary
Customer-side alignment was confirmed, with Scott validating the agreement in principle, although legal compliance review remained pending. The order form had been fully realigned, with requested items addressed and no additions identified; further platform use cases and deeper adoption were encouraged through QBRs. Legal flagged the AI training clause because of sensitive-data concerns, and removal of the AI provision was approved without an expected review restart. The customer also requested removal of data-retention language related to the AI clause, including aggregated-data wording. Questions about external product restrictions and feature-flag resale were addressed by explaining that agency protections cover marketing agencies and prevent client resale. The AI clause was described as the only blocker. A revised agreement was expected shortly, followed by DocuSign routing to Scott, with Ahmed, Florian, and Rémi copied. Finalization was targeted for Friday, pending the legal response and Scott’s approval. (Sources: 01:52–08:20)

## Keywords
Contract finalisation, Legal compliance, AI data training, Data retention, DocuSign, Feature flags

## Action Items
**Kpler Legal and Compliance**
Review revised customer agreement (03:22)

**Marcel Geldner**
Remove AI-training provision (06:46)
Remove data-retention language (06:53)

**James Shannon**
Send revised customer agreement (07:45)

**Scott**
Sign agreement through DocuSign (08:04)
